title: Why Billionaires Take a $1 Salary 💵 #shorts
description:
Mark Zuckerberg has taken a $1 salary since 2013, and Steve Jobs took $1 a year at Apple. Their wealth sits in shares: US salary is taxed up to 37% every year, while share gains aren't taxed until they're sold.
Source: Meta 2026 proxy statement (SEC Form DEF 14A); Quartz & NBC News (2013); NBC News & CNN Money on Steve Jobs; Tax Foundation & NerdWallet 2026 tax brackets. Education, not financial advice.
script: Mark Zuckerberg's salary is one dollar a year, and it has been since twenty thirteen.
Steve Jobs took one dollar a year at Apple too.
So are billionaires just being generous?
Not really. Their real money sits in their company's shares.
A salary gets taxed every year, at up to thirty-seven percent federal tax in America.
But shares that grow aren't taxed until you sell them.
And a one dollar salary tells investors: I only get rich if you get rich.
Your salary pays the bills. What you own builds the wealth.
